CausalChain: Overexpression of nuclear lncRNA MALAT1 -> Alters transcriptional programs and metabolic regulators in cancer cells -> Disrupts mitochondrial integrity and function -> Leads to altered expression/processing of mitochondrial ASncmtRNAs -> Changes in mitochondrial miRNA release and apoptotic signaling -> Formation of a feedback loop that reinforces metabolic reprogramming and chemoresistance
Hypothesis: A synergistic interplay between nuclear lncRNA MALAT1 and mitochondrial ASncmtRNAs establishes a regulatory feedback loop that modulates tumor cell metabolism and drug resistance. Concurrently targeting both nuclear and mitochondrial lncRNA pathways may disrupt this loop, reprogram tumor bioenergetics, and overcome chemoresistance.
Abstract: Recent studies have revealed that long non‐coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play pivotal roles in gene regulation, tumor metabolism, and drug resistance. Building on evidence that nuclear lncRNAs, such as MALAT1, drive oncogenic gene expression and modulate cellular metabolic pathways, and that mitochondrial lncRNAs (mtlncRNAs) like ASncmtRNAs regulate mitochondrial function and apoptotic signaling, we propose a novel inter-compartmental regulatory network whereby nuclear and mitochondrial lncRNAs form a feedback loop that contributes to metabolic reprogramming and therapeutic resistance in cancer cells. This abstract outlines a testable hypothesis that a coordinated cross-talk between nuclear and mitochondrial lncRNAs regulates the bioenergetic state of cancer cells and that dual modulation of these lncRNAs could sensitize tumors to conventional therapies.
